definitions.text: A logical time interval provided by joined federates that become time-regulating. When added to the time-regulating joined federate's time position, the resulting timestamp is used to calculate the bound on the timestamps that the time-regulating joined federate can use to send timestamp order (TSO) messages.
definitions.layout_body: A logical time interval provided by joined federates that become time-regulating. definitions.text: A previously joined federate that has been disconnected from the runtime infrastructure (RTI) as a result of a fault so that the joined federate can no longer continue in the federation execution in a High Level Architecture (HLA) compliant manner.
definitions.layout_body: A previously joined federate that has been disconnected from the runtime infrastructure (RTI) as a result of a fault so that the joined federate can no longer continue in the federation execution in a High Level Architecture (HLA) compliant manner.

definitions.text: A group of predefined High Level Architecture (HLA) constructs (object and interaction classes) that provide the following: [32.04pt] ; Access to federation execution operating information ; Insight into the operations of joined federates and the runtime infrastructure (RTI) ; Control of the functioning of the RTI, the federation execution, and the individual joined federates
definitions.layout_body:
A group of predefined High Level Architecture (HLA) constructs (object and interaction classes) that provide the following:
\begin{hladefinitionlistroomy}[32.04pt]
\item Access to federation execution operating information
\item Insight into the operations of joined federates and the runtime infrastructure (RTI)
\item Control of the functioning of the RTI, the federation execution, and the individual joined federates
\end{hladefinitionlistroomy}

definitions.term: Management Object Model (MOM) and Initialization Module (MIM)
definitions.text: A subset of the federation object model (FOM) that contains object model template (OMT) tables that describe the High Level Architecture (HLA) MOM. The MIM also contains additional predefined HLA constructs such as object and interaction roots, data types, transportation types, and dimensions. HLA specifies a standard MIM that is incorporated into all FOM Document Data (FDD) automatically by the runtime infrastructure (RTI). The standard MIM can be replaced with a user-supplied MIM containing the standard MIM plus extensions.

definitions.text: A change of object instance attribute value(s), an interaction, a directed interaction, or a deletion of an existing object instance, often associated with a particular point on the time axis, as denoted by the associated timestamp.
definitions.layout_body: A change of object instance attribute value(s), an interaction, a directed interaction, or a deletion of an existing object instance, often associated with a particular point on the time axis, as denoted by the associated timestamp.

definitions.text: A designator reserved to indicate an empty value that is distinguishable from all other designators. A null designator is guaranteed to compare unequal to any other designator with a nonempty value.
definitions.layout_body: A designator reserved to indicate an empty value that is distinguishable from all other designators. A null designator is guaranteed to compare unequal to any other designator with a nonempty value.

definitions.text: A fundamental element of a conceptual representation for a federate that reflects the real world at levels of abstraction and resolution appropriate for federate interoperability. An object class is a template for a set of characteristics that is common to a group of object instances. These characteristics correspond to the class attributes and class directed interactions that individual federates may publish and to which other federates may subscribe.

definitions.text: A unique instantiation of an object class that is independent of all other instances of that object class. At any point during a federation execution, the state of a High Level Architecture (HLA) object instance is defined as the collection of the values of all its instance attributes.
definitions.layout_body: A unique instantiation of an object class that is independent of all other instances of that object class. definitions.text: A system specification defined primarily by class characteristics and relationships. The High Level Architecture (HLA) idea of an object model is similar in many ways, but not identical, to the common idea of an object model in object-oriented literature.

definitions.text: The rules and terminology used to describe High Level Architecture (HLA) object models.

definitions.text: A supplementary logical time that facilitates optimistic time advancement. The optimistic logical time is provided, along with the update to the federate's logical time, in a Flush Queue Grant service call as a response to a Flush Queue Request service call. It is the minimum of the time supplied in the Flush Queue Request and the timestamps of any TSO messages delivered in response to that Flush Queue Request. The optimistic logical time indicates a lower bound on the next logical time the federate could be advanced to if no TSO messages with a timestamp less than it are received in the future.
definitions.layout_body: A supplementary logical time that facilitates optimistic time advancement. The optimistic logical time is provided, along with the update to the federate's logical time, in a \HLAService{Flush Queue Grant} \HLAPrintersDagger{} service call as a response to a \HLAService{Flush Queue Request} service call. It is the minimum of the time supplied in the \HLAService{Flush Queue Request} and the timestamps of any TSO messages delivered in response to that \HLAService{Flush Queue Request}. The optimistic logical time indicates a lower bound on the next logical time the federate could be advanced to if no TSO messages with a timestamp less than it are received in the future.

definitions.text: The lookahead the federate would have if actually granted to the optimistic logical time.
definitions.layout_body: The lookahead the federate would have if actually granted to the optimistic logical time.

definitions.text: A runtime infrastructure (RTI) means of ordering messages originating from multiple joined federates that are delivered to a single joined federate. Different categories of service are defined with different characteristics regarding whether and how an RTI orders messages that are to be delivered to a joined federate.

definitions.text: Of or pertaining to an instance attribute of an object instance for which one or more of the following are not true: [32.04pt] ; The object instance is known to the joined federate. ; The instance attribute is owned by another joined federate. ; The instance attribute's corresponding class attribute is one of the following: [22.02pt] ; A subscribed attribute of the known class of the object instance, or ; A subscribed attribute of the known class of the object instance with regions, and the update region set of the instance attribute at the owning joined federate overlaps the subscription region set of the instance attribute's corresponding class attribute at the known class of the instance attribute at the subscribing joined federate. % 9pt10.8pt NOTE---See 6.1 of IEEE Std 1516.1-2025.
definitions.layout_body:
Of or pertaining to an instance attribute of an object instance for which one or more of the following are not true:
\vspace*{2.13pt}
\begin{hladefinitionlist}[32.04pt]
\item The object instance is known to the joined federate.
\item The instance attribute is owned by another joined federate.
\item The instance attribute's corresponding class attribute is one of the following:
 \begin{hladefinitionnumberlist}[22.02pt]
 \item A subscribed attribute of the known class of the object instance, or
 \item A subscribed attribute of the known class of the object instance with regions, and the update region set of the instance attribute at the owning joined federate overlaps the subscription region set of the instance attribute's corresponding class attribute at the known class of the instance attribute at the subscribing joined federate.
 \end{hladefinitionnumberlist}
\end{hladefinitionlist}
\par\addvspace{12.49pt}%
\hspace*{49.68pt}{\fontsize{9pt}{10.8pt}\selectfont NOTE---See 6.1 of IEEE Std 1516.1\HLAStandardMark-2025.}\par

definitions.text: [32.40pt] ; Pertaining to region sets: given two region sets, to have a region in each set such that the two regions overlap. ; Pertaining to regions: given two regions, to have at least one dimension in common if and only if, for each dimension, the regions have in common, their respective ranges in the common dimension overlap. If two regions do not have any dimensions in common, the regions do not overlap. ; Pertaining to ranges: given two ranges (\(A = [a_lower, a_upper)\) and \(B = [b_lower, b_upper)\)), to overlap if and only if [22.02pt] ; Either \(a_lower = b_lower\) or (\(a_lower < b_upper\) and \(b_lower < a_upper\)) or ; The Allow Relaxed DDM switch is enabled and the RTI implementation makes the determination, based on implementation-specific criteria, that the ranges are sufficiently close to warrant an expanded interpretation of one or both ranges neither range may ever be reduced. % 9pt10.8pt NOTE---See 9.1 of IEEE Std 1516.1-2025.
definitions.layout_body:
\vspace*{2.13pt}
\begin{hladefinitionlist}[32.40pt]
\item Pertaining to region sets: given two region sets, to have a region in each set such that the two regions overlap.
\item Pertaining to regions: given two regions, to have at least one dimension in common if and only if, for each dimension, the regions have in common, their respective ranges in the common dimension overlap. If two regions do not have any dimensions in common, the regions do not overlap.
\item Pertaining to ranges: given two ranges (\(A = [a_{\mathrm{lower}}, a_{\mathrm{upper}})\) and \(B = [b_{\mathrm{lower}}, b_{\mathrm{upper}})\)), to overlap if and only if
 \begin{hladefinitionnumberlist}[22.02pt]
 \item Either \(a_{\mathrm{lower}} = b_{\mathrm{lower}}\) or (\(a_{\mathrm{lower}} < b_{\mathrm{upper}}\) and \(b_{\mathrm{lower}} < a_{\mathrm{upper}}\)) or
 \item The Allow Relaxed DDM switch is enabled and the RTI implementation makes the determination, based on implementation-specific criteria, that the ranges are sufficiently close to warrant an expanded interpretation of one or both ranges\HLASemicolon{} neither range may ever be reduced.
 \end{hladefinitionnumberlist}
\end{hladefinitionlist}
\par\vspace*{-9.41pt}%
\hspace*{28.02pt}{\fontsize{9pt}{10.8pt}\selectfont NOTE---See 9.1 of IEEE Std 1516.1\HLAStandardMark-2025.}\par

All pairs within the passel have the same user-supplied tag, sent message order type, transportation type, receive message order type, timestamp (if present), and set of sent region designators (if present). A passel is a message.

definitions.text: A request to the runtime infrastructure (RTI) for the kinds of data (object classes and attributes as well as interactions) that the joined federate is currently interested in receiving. However, unlike an active subscription, this information is not used by the RTI to arrange for data to be delivered, nor is it used to tell publishing joined federates that another joined federate is subscribing to that data (by way of Start/Stop Registration, Turn On/Off Updates, or Turn On/Off Interactions service invocations). This form of subscription is provided to support certain types of logger joined federates.

definitions.text: The interval between a joined federate's request to advance its time position and the corresponding grant by the runtime infrastructure (RTI). A joined federate may advance its time position only by requesting a time advancement from the RTI via one of the following services: ; Time Advance Request ; Time Advance Request Available ; Next Message Request ; Next Message Request Available ; Flush Queue Request The joined federate's time position will not actually be advanced until the RTI responds with a Time Advance Grant or Flush Queue Grant service invocation at that joined federate.

A totally ordered sequence of discrete values in which each value typically represents an HLA instant of time in the physical system being modeled. For any two points, T1 and T2, on the time axis, if T1 < T2, T1 represents an instant of time that occurs before the instant represented by T2. The sequence begins with an initial value, for which no point is less, and ends with a final value, for which no point is greater.
